title: Phishing Attack Simulation
description: A simulation designed for corporate security training to help employees recognize and respond to phishing attempts. It models the process of a targeted phishing campaign, from reconnaissance to payload delivery.
objective: To simulate a targeted phishing campaign from reconnaissance to payload delivery, for the purpose of training and security awareness.
principles: Phishing is a social engineering attack that uses deception to trick users into revealing sensitive information (like passwords or credit card numbers) or to deploy malicious software. It relies on creating a sense of urgency, trust, or authority by impersonating a legitimate entity.

steps.title: Target Reconnaissance
steps.action: Gather information about the target organization and its employees from public sources like social media (e.g., LinkedIn) and the company website.
steps.detail: This information (e.g., names, job titles, email formats) is used to craft a highly convincing and personalized phishing email, a technique known as 'spear phishing'.

steps.title: Craft the Phishing Email
steps.action: Create a fraudulent email that appears to be from a legitimate source, such as a trusted colleague, the IT department, or a known vendor.
steps.detail: The email will contain a compelling call to action, such as a warning that an account will be suspended or an offer for a free product, to entice the user to click a malicious link.

steps.title: Clone the Login Page
steps.action: Create a pixel-perfect clone of a legitimate website's login page, such as a corporate portal, webmail client, or bank website.
steps.detail: This page will be hosted on a server controlled by the attacker. The URL will often be disguised using URL shorteners or look-alike domains (typosquatting).

steps.title: Deploy the Campaign
steps.action: Send the phishing email to the targeted employees, often using a spoofed 'From' address to increase its appearance of legitimacy.
steps.detail: The email will contain a link to the cloned login page. The campaign is often timed to coincide with real-world events to increase its believability.

steps.title: Harvest Credentials
steps.action: When an employee clicks the link and enters their credentials on the fake login page, the information is captured and stored on the attacker's server.
steps.detail: The fake page will typically redirect the user to the real website after they submit their information, to avoid arousing suspicion.

steps.title: Deliver Payload & Obfuscate (Optional)
steps.action: After harvesting credentials, the user can be redirected to the legitimate website, or a malicious payload (e.g., ransomware, spyware) can be downloaded to their machine.
steps.detail: This simulation concludes with a report of compromised credentials and provides educational material on how the attack could have been prevented.

tips: Always hover over links in emails to check the actual destination URL before clicking.
Be wary of emails that create a sense of urgency or demand immediate action. This is a common tactic to bypass critical thinking.
